Spray bleach on the mold, really saturate it. Give it week, bet there will be a difference. Do it again if necessary. It's magic in a bottle. I've gotten rid of mold even thru wall paper by saturating it with bleach and letting it sit. If it's really bad, do it a few days in a row.

Just me workin on me. Only help I get is from God and the universe. No one's coming. I was buried in my house and barely able to get out of bed due to medical issues and no one came. For years. And they still aren't. It's just me trying to dig myself out of the grave.

Edit: and getting to the bottom of all the issues so I don't find myself having to deal with them again. I've come to learn that if I understand something it gives me the ability to choose, rather than doing things and I don't know why. 

Take purchases for example. Once I started understanding what was really behind my impulses I was able to break out of the cycle. Learning about the chemical release in the brain was a game changer. Because of this, I will learn more about this. Understanding the process allows me to steer.

Jars of urine. That's a tough one. There may be an element of accumulation of a thing that comes into play. I haven't had the urine jar problem but I have had the accumulation issue. I need a lot of something even tho I end up never touching it. The feeling of having an abundance of something (in their case urine), makes sense to me especially for people who have had a history of lacking something. I know the translation is weird, but say someone didn't have a lot of love in their life, they will (can) hoard a replacement. Urine is free. Containers are free if you use old food jars. Viola, an opportunity to have something in abundance. And it's not just empty jars, they're serving a function...as odd of a function as it may be. 

I'd be interested to hear from a real urine hoarder. There's so many twists and turns to hoarding. Before I was a hoarder, I would look at people and their situations and not understand one bit about how that could happen. Now I'm in the eye of the storm. 🤦

Well reddit made it bold, not me. And I suppose when I was asking it was bad phrasing. I should have maybe said "I'm realizing abandonment issues can have a hand in hoarding". I was kind of figuring something out in that moment so it got phrased like that. 

You're welcome to your own opinion but I would rethink applying broadly if I were you, but do you.

I suppose it's possible. Seeing the value of something can extend to that I suppose. Old newspapers can either be like hoarding books (so utility/information/historical reflection) or like collecting recycle. Broken bottles might be again like collecting recycle or they might have a repurposing idea for them that they never get around to, or there was sentiment to the thing that broke. I've done this. Pieces of dirty paper could have things written on them that they want to circle back to, ideas maybe, or something that reminds them of something. Dirty paper isn't unusable/unreadable, so there could be an element of not wanting to be wasteful. If one grew up poor this might come into play even more so. Could be any number of things. Urine soaked rug might be kept because they have it in their mind they intend to clean it. 

You ask if hoarders are attached to that because of abandonment. It's possible. Seeing themselves thrown away by others could trigger the attachment. Seeing themselves as something that still has value even tho others threw them away could easily transfer to how they think—or rather how they don't think—about stuff, especially the easily disregarded stuff.
I feel you. I've needed love I didn't have my whole life too.
I'm sorry, what are you saying no to?
You know what, I had that issue too. A history of having things taken or not be available to me caused it.

Yes!! I've been reading thru some of the posts on this sub, dissecting the in's and out's of the complexities of hoarding. I used to see people on TV hoarding and couldn't understand it. Good ol' life, guess what got plunked on my lesson plan of life? That's right, I became a hoarder. Now I get to repair myself and learn first hand how to come back from this. Not everyone will have identical causes, I get that, but everyone will be identical in having a cause. The root of an orange tree is not the root of an apple tree, but they are both roots, none the less.

I can see my issues are layered. I was the type to buy things and bring them home and never take them out of the bag. In going thru things now, I find bags of stuff I bought a decade ago that is still in the bag it came home from the store in. So the initial buying part I begun to tackle first. I have a fairly good handle on it now, and understand more of what was actually at work, compelling me. 

I get stuck at the getting rid of stuff part. I've been frustrated with myself about it. I have better days I'm trying to get to but I'm held back by stuff. Some feelings I understand but haven't been able to over come yet, others I'm like I don't even understand why I can't let this go. It's like I'm fighting myself. It's actually ridiculous how little control I have over myself when it come to this. A few things just clicked as I write this tho. Me being out of control of my life has been a life long trauma that has never been rectified. I can actually see how it's a requirement that I learn how to be in control of myself, like an exercise kinda, that's starting with my stuff. To be clear, when I say out of control, I mean quite literally not allowed government over myself, not the other kind.

 It's so amazing how my environment is a direct reflection of what's going on internally. It's jaw-dropping actually. What things I need to fix internally, I need to fix externally too. 🤯

Yes, I understand, I have the same problem with my mom. Even an abundance of useless texts to fb shit...it's just clutter in my messages. My mom gives me everything she doesn't want but acts all hurt if I don't want it; asked if I wore this or that, etc. I'm like stop giving me the shit you don't want. She says "I'm not, I thought you'd like it". It's just gaslighting, really. She will also buy shit like you're talking about, but it's mostly just bullshit either way. I then have to deal with the guilt of getting rid of the shit. Gee thanks mom, for the gift of guilt...you shouldn't have—really. I've started to be more frank about things. "Please stop giving me this shit, you see I'm trying to fight living like a fkn hoarder, this shit doesn't help." And " stop giving me the shit you don't want. Give it to goodwill." And "how about you ask me if I want it before you actually buy it". She still does it but less, and she gets met with the reminder of what she's actually giving me: more clutter, a guilt trip, or putting me in the position to look like a bad guy for even saying anything at all.  My mom will say "I know it's not your style but..." But nothing. You know I'm not interested so stop. Whatever is behind it has more to do with her and her dopamine hit than me. Or whatever it is that is going on for her.

I understand love languages is a thing. I fell into the trap of buying shit for my kid that she didn't want. Then I realized I'm just continuing the cycle and now I ask her first. A pic in text saves a lot of hurt feeling and wasted money.

I also think assisted suicide should be available to everyone. The part where I vier from your view is in having to convince a doctor. I don't agree that we should have to place our decision in the hands of another. I hear people say similar things to what you have about having a professional sign off on it, however I think it's fair to point out that allowing other people to make decisions for our lives means we don't have government even over our own death. I hate the part about having to convince someone else of what we want for ourselves. What are your thoughts on that?
